score_rationale: Exceptional commercial validation with at least 6 active B2B database vendors currently selling nonprofit executive and board director contact lists: NonProfitLists.com (transparent pricing at $379 for 1.65M organizations with 493,340 direct emails, lifetime access no subscription), InfoGlobalData (nonprofit CEOs, board members, development directors, program officers), Blue Mail Media (all-in-one database with names, emails, phones, social media, specializations), Hippo Direct (executive directors, program directors, chief development officers, fundraising executives), FountMedia (30-45 day update cycle), LeadsPlease (verified lists for B2B vendors, fundraisers, service providers), and AmeriList (proprietary Charitable Giving Index Score for donor targeting). Market size is massive: IRS EO BMF contains 1,923,040+ active tax-exempt organizations as of November 2025, with ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer enabling search across millions of annual returns including officer/director/trustee compensation data from Form 990 Part VII. Five exceptionally high-value B2B buyer segments with validated LTV justification: (1) Fundraising software vendors (Bloomerang at $99-$499/month, DonorPerfect at $89-$329/month, Blackbaud Raiser's Edge NXT at $3,000-$30,000/year, Keela, Givebutter) selling mission-critical donor management platforms to nonprofits at $1,000-$30,000/year subscriptions where one acquired customer generates 2.5×-75× ROI vs. $379 database cost and customer lifetime value of $10,000-$300,000 over 10-year nonprofit software retention cycles; (2) Grant consulting firms billing $5,000-$50,000 per grant application (typical federal grants $50K-$5M, foundation grants $10K-$500K) where a single consulting engagement justifies 13×-132× database investment and one client relationship often spans multiple grant cycles generating $20,000-$200,000 in total fees; (3) Board management SaaS platforms (Boardable at $79-$329/month, BoardEffect at $12,000-$25,000/year, Diligent Boards, OnBoard) selling governance software to nonprofit boards at $1,000-$25,000/year where one enterprise nonprofit account = 2.6×-66× database cost ROI; (4) Professional services specialized for nonprofits (CPA firms providing Form 990 preparation and nonprofit audits at $3,000-$25,000/year, employment law attorneys, HR consultants for nonprofit compensation studies, fractional CFO services at $2,000-$10,000/month) where one client generates $3,000-$120,000/year in recurring revenue = 7.9×-316× ROI; (5) Vendor suppliers to nonprofits (event planning and catering for fundraising galas, insurance brokers selling D&O coverage for board members at $2,000-$15,000/year, commercial real estate brokers for nonprofit office space, AV/tech vendors for conference centers, marketing agencies for capital campaigns). Total addressable market of 1.9M+ tax-exempt organizations includes 360,000+ 501(c)(3) public charities with annual revenue over $50,000 (medium-to-large nonprofits most likely to purchase software/services), generating estimated 500,000-750,000 decision-maker contacts (executive directors, development directors, CFOs, board chairs, program VPs) across healthcare nonprofits, educational institutions, religious organizations, human services agencies, arts/culture organizations, environmental groups, and advocacy nonprofits. Public data is 100% accessible and authoritative: IRS requires all tax-exempt organizations to file annual Form 990 returns (public disclosure mandated by law), with Part VII Section A listing all officers, directors, trustees, key employees, and five highest compensated employees including names, titles, and compensation — available as bulk XML downloads from IRS Form 990 Series Downloads (organized by year and month, electronically filed 990s since 2010), ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer (searchable people database updated April 2026 enabling 'search for a person' across all 990 filings to find individuals serving on multiple boards), and state charity registration databases maintained by Attorneys General offices (additional contact details, EINs, registration status). Engineering lift is moderate: download IRS 990 XML bulk files, parse Part VII to extract officer/director/trustee records, cross-reference with IRS EO BMF for organization metadata (revenue, assets, NTEE codes, subsector classification), supplement with state AG charity registries for additional contacts/validation, normalize job titles (Executive Director vs CEO vs President, Development Director vs Chief Development Officer), deduplicate individuals serving on multiple boards, geocode mailing addresses, classify by nonprofit subsector and revenue tier. No affordable flat-file competitor exists below $379 on Gumroad — NonProfitLists.com is the ONLY transparent one-time-purchase vendor (all others use enterprise 'contact sales for quote' pricing typical of B2B list brokers at $0.15-$0.50 per contact = $7,500-$25,000 for 50,000-record targeted list), making a $149-$199 instant-download CSV deliver 50-62% cost savings vs. NonProfitLists.com and 97-99% savings vs. traditional per-contact enterprise pricing. Score is 8 due to: (a) strong commercial ecosystem with 6+ active vendors and sustained demand across multiple buyer verticals, (b) exceptionally high buyer LTV across all five segments (fundraising software $10K-$300K lifetime, grant consulting $20K-$200K per client, board management SaaS $10K-$250K lifetime, professional services $30K-$1.2M over 10 years, vendor suppliers $2K-$150K/year recurring) where one customer acquisition justifies 5×-3,160× database cost, (c) massive TAM (1.9M organizations, 500K-750K decision-makers), (d) 100% public and authoritative data via federally mandated IRS 990 disclosures with bulk download access, (e) moderate engineering complexity (XML parsing, deduplication, title normalization), and (f) significant pricing wedge opportunity vs. both NonProfitLists.com ($379) and traditional enterprise vendors ($7,500-$25,000). Score not higher due to: (a) one existing transparent competitor (NonProfitLists.com) already serving this exact market at $379 baseline, requiring our product to deliver clear differentiation via superior data quality (more email enrichment, phone number coverage), additional fields (board tenure, donation history flags, program focus areas), or more aggressive pricing ($149-$199 undercuts by 50-62%) to justify purchase vs. established vendor.
summary: A comprehensive CSV of all U.S. nonprofit organization executives and board members extracted from IRS Form 990 tax filings (Part VII: Officers, Directors, Trustees, Key Employees), cross-referenced with IRS Exempt Organizations Business Master File and state charity registration databases. Each record includes individual name, job title (Executive Director, Board Chair, Development Director, CFO, Program Director, Treasurer, Secretary, Trustee), organization legal name, EIN, mailing address, phone, email (where available via public filings or state registries), organization revenue tier, asset value, nonprofit subsector (NTEE classification: healthcare, education, human services, arts/culture, environment, religion, advocacy), geographic region, and years in role (where disclosed). As of November 2025, the IRS EO BMF contained 1,923,040+ active tax-exempt organizations across all 50 states, with approximately 360,000 public charities reporting annual revenue over $50,000 (medium-to-large nonprofits most likely to purchase B2B software and professional services). Target output: 500,000-750,000 decision-maker contact records spanning executive directors, chief development officers, board chairs, CFOs, program VPs, and trustees across 501(c)(3) public charities, 501(c)(4) social welfare organizations, 501(c)(6) business leagues, and other tax-exempt entities. Five exceptionally high-value B2B buyer segments: (1) Fundraising software vendors (Bloomerang $99-$499/month, DonorPerfect $89-$329/month, Blackbaud Raiser's Edge NXT $3K-$30K/year, Keela, Givebutter) selling donor management and online giving platforms at $1,000-$30,000/year subscriptions where one acquired customer = 2.6×-79× database cost ROI and 10-year customer lifetime value of $10,000-$300,000; (2) Grant consulting firms billing $5,000-$50,000 per grant application (federal grants $50K-$5M, foundation grants $10K-$500K) where single engagement = 13×-132× ROI and multi-year client relationships generate $20,000-$200,000 total fees; (3) Board management SaaS (Boardable $79-$329/month, BoardEffect $12K-$25K/year, Diligent, OnBoard) selling governance software at $1,000-$25,000/year where one enterprise account = 2.6×-66× ROI; (4) Professional services for nonprofits (CPA firms for 990 prep and audits $3K-$25K/year, employment lawyers, HR consultants, fractional CFOs $2K-$10K/month) where one client = 7.9×-316× database cost ROI and generates $3,000-$120,000/year recurring; (5) Vendor suppliers (event planners for galas, D&O insurance brokers $2K-$15K/year, commercial real estate, AV/tech, capital campaign marketing agencies). A one-time $149-$199 CSV undercuts NonProfitLists.com ($379 for similar dataset) by 50-62% and delivers 97-99% savings vs. traditional B2B list brokers charging $0.15-$0.50 per contact ($7,500-$25,000 for 50K targeted records), providing complete nonprofit executive TAM for fundraising software, grant consultants, board management platforms, professional services, and vendor suppliers.

data_wanted: IRS Form 990 Series filings (all tax-exempt organizations with gross receipts >= $50,000 must file annually) provide comprehensive officer and director data in Part VII Section A: name, title (officer, director, trustee, key employee, highest compensated employee), hours per week, reportable compensation, other compensation. IRS publishes bulk XML downloads at irs.gov/charities-non-profits/form-990-series-downloads organized by year (filings from 2010-present) and by month for current year — electronically filed 990s include complete structured data in machine-readable XML format. IRS Exempt Organizations Business Master File Extract (EO BMF) at irs.gov/charities-non-profits/exempt-organizations-business-master-file-extract-eo-bmf contains 1,923,040+ records (as of November 2025) with organization metadata: EIN, legal name, DBA, mailing address, state, ZIP, ruling date, asset amount, income amount, NTEE classification code (26 major categories × 10 subcategories = 260 nonprofit types including hospitals A, higher education B, human services P, arts/culture A, environment C, religion X), foundation code (private foundation vs public charity vs supporting organization), and tax period. ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer at projects.propublica.org/nonprofits provides searchable interface to millions of 990 returns with 'People Search' feature (launched 2018, updated April 2026) enabling lookup of individuals across all filings to identify board members serving on multiple nonprofit boards — database includes executive compensation, revenue, expenses, and full text search of filings. State-level charity registration databases maintained by Attorneys General offices (all 50 states require registration for nonprofits soliciting donations, with state-specific filing requirements): California Attorney General Registry of Charitable Trusts, New York Charities Bureau, Massachusetts AGO Non-Profit Organizations/Public Charities Division, Texas Secretary of State Charitable Organizations database, Florida Division of Consumer Services Solicitation of Contributions registry — these often include additional contact information beyond IRS filings such as primary contact email, phone, responsible officer name, registered agent, website URL. Target fields per record: Individual name (first, middle, last), job title/position (normalize to standard taxonomy: Executive Director/CEO, Board Chair/President, Development Director/Chief Development Officer, CFO/Treasurer, Program Director/COO, Secretary, Trustee/Director, VP of Programs, VP of Finance), organization legal name, organization DBA/common name, EIN, organization mailing address (street, city, state, ZIP), organization phone, organization email (from state filings or website), organization website, individual email (where available in state registries or via LinkedIn/ZoomInfo enrichment), nonprofit subsector (NTEE code and human-readable category), annual revenue tier (<$100K, $100K-$500K, $500K-$1M, $1M-$5M, $5M-$10M, $10M+), total assets, foundation type (public charity 501c3, private foundation, social welfare 501c4, trade association 501c6, other), geographic region, tax year of most recent filing, years in current role (where disclosed). Target all decision-makers: C-suite executives (CEO, CFO, COO, CDO), board leadership (Chair, Vice Chair, Treasurer, Secretary), development/fundraising staff (Chief Development Officer, Director of Development, Major Gifts Officer, Grants Manager), and program leadership (VP of Programs, Program Directors). Estimated 500,000-750,000 total contact records spanning 360,000+ nonprofits with revenue over $50,000 (medium-to-large organizations most likely to purchase software/services, excluding smallest all-volunteer nonprofits under $50K revenue). Data is 100% public: federal law requires disclosure of Form 990 returns under IRC Section 6104, IRS provides free bulk downloads, ProPublica mirrors all filings, and state charity registrations are public records under state sunshine laws — no authentication barriers, no paywalls, no FOIA requests needed for core regulatory data (though email enrichment may require supplemental business directory lookups or LinkedIn scraping to enhance IRS/state base records).

willingness_to_pay.signal: Five buyer segments with exceptional LTV justification and confirmed commercial demand (6+ vendors actively selling nonprofit databases): (1) Fundraising software vendors: Annual SaaS subscriptions at $1,000-$30,000/year (Bloomerang, DonorPerfect, Blackbaud) generate $10,000-$300,000 customer lifetime value over 10-year nonprofit software retention cycles, making $149-$199 database cost deliver 50×-1,500× ROI when five customers are acquired through targeted outreach to development directors at mid-size charities ($500K-$5M revenue tier most likely to purchase donor management platforms). Mission-critical nature of fundraising software (nonprofits cannot operate without donor tracking and online giving capabilities) creates high conversion rates and minimal price sensitivity for database acquisition costs under $200. (2) Grant consulting firms: Single federal grant application at $10,000-$50,000 in consulting fees for $500K-$5M SAMHSA/HHS/DOE awards justifies $149-$199 database cost 50×-250×, and multi-year client relationships across multiple grant cycles (federal grants often span 3-5 years with annual continuation applications, foundation grants renew biannually) generate $20,000-$200,000 cumulative fees per client = 100×-1,000× database ROI. Nonprofits actively seek grant writers (88% of nonprofits pursue grants but only 34% have dedicated grant staff per 2024 Grants Plus survey), creating high inbound demand. (3) Board management SaaS: Enterprise contracts at $12,000-$25,000/year for large healthcare systems, universities, and foundations (BoardEffect, Diligent) generate $120,000-$250,000 lifetime value over 10-year governance platform retention, making $149-$199 database trivial when two enterprise customers are acquired = 120×-1,250× ROI. Sarbanes-Oxley-style governance requirements and fiduciary duty concerns drive board software adoption at well-funded nonprofits. (4) Professional services: CPA firms earn $5,000-$25,000/year recurring revenue per nonprofit audit client (required for organizations over $750K revenue per federal Single Audit Act), making one client acquisition = 25×-125× database cost, and 10-year client relationships generate $50,000-$250,000 cumulative fees. Form 990 preparation and nonprofit audits are non-discretionary compliance expenses creating captive market. (5) Vendor suppliers: D&O insurance brokers earn $400-$3,000 in annual commissions per nonprofit client (20% of $2,000-$15,000 premium), event planners bill $15,000-$250,000 per fundraising gala, and capital campaign marketing agencies charge $30,000-$300,000 per campaign — all segments justify 75×-1,500× database investment when multiple clients are acquired. NonProfitLists.com's $379 transparent pricing establishes baseline willingness-to-pay (1.65M organizations with 493K emails = $0.23 per record for comprehensive dataset), confirming strong market acceptance of flat-file purchases vs. traditional B2B list brokers charging $0.15-$0.50 per contact ($7,500-$25,000 for 50,000 targeted records). Opportunity to undercut NonProfitLists.com by 50-62% at $149-$199 while potentially offering superior data quality (higher email coverage via state registry enrichment, phone number fields, board tenure data) creates compelling value proposition for all five buyer segments.
